* In [[Pakistan]], a bill proposing to strengthen the law against "[[Honour Killing]]" is defeated in [[Parliament of Pakistan|Parliament]], after the government sides with the [[Islamist]] opposition and deems the bill "un-Islamic". [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/4311055.stm (BBC)]
* Unpopular [[Chief Executive of Hong Kong|Chief Executive]] [[Tung Chee-hwa]] of the former [[British overseas territory|British colony]] of [[Hong Kong]] reportedly resigns, with reluctant approval from [[Beijing]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20051128141700/http://www.thestandard.com.hk/stdn/std/Front_Page/GC02Aa01.html (The Standard)], [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/4310235.stm (BBC)],[https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/hong-kong-s-leader-to-step-down-reports-1.537253 (CBC)], [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/story/RTGAM.20050302.wchtung0302/BNStory/International/ (Globe&Mail)], [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=7782051 (Reuters)]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, [http://edition.cnn.com/2005/WORLD/asiapcf/03/02/hongkong.tung/ (CNN)],   [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/4310407.stm (BBC)]. 
* [[Banda Sea earthquake]]: An [[earthquake]] measuring up to 7.5 on the [[Richter scale]] hits [[Darwin, Northern Territory]] in [[Australia]] [https://web.archive.org/web/20060107180652/http://www.abc.net.au/news/newsitems/200503/s1314649.htm (ABC News)]
* The [[Israeli Defence Forces]] discover a [[Hamas]] bomb-lab near [[Jenin]] in a metal workshop.  The lab contains what appeared to be a [[Qassam rocket]] in an initial state of production, and large quantities of other materials used for manufacturing bombs. [http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/547051.html (Haaretz)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* US company [[Titan Corporation]] agrees to pay a [[Fine (penalty)|fine]] equivalent to [[US$]]28.5 million after they admit attempting [[bribery]] to get a [[military communications]] contract in [[Benin]]. The corporation allegedly gave US$2 million to the re-election campaign of president [[Mathieu Kérékou]].  [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=7779972 (Reuters)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050305065838/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=7779972 |date=2005-03-05 }}, [http://news.ft.com/cms/s/5891c8ae-8ab1-11d9-9059-00000e2511c8.html (Financial Times)], [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/4310331.stm (BBC)]
* [[Microsoft]] founder [[Bill Gates]] is awarded the title of [[Knight Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire]] by Queen [[Elizabeth II]] (which will entitle him to suffix the letters "KBE" to his name but not use the title of "Sir") for his contribution to enterprise in the United Kingdom and his efforts in [[poverty]] reduction around the world. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/3428673.stm (BBC)]
